parts:
Hi Grace,

You need to use the names of your covariates -- which appear to be "x1", "x2", "x3" -- not "siteCovs" and "obsCovs". Try this:

occu(~x1 + x2 + x3 ~ x1 + x2, umf)
occu(~x3 ~ x1, umf)

Richard

Hi Grace,

Did you notice that x1 and x2 are identical? The hessian will always be singular in such a case. Also, have you seen the help pages found by typing:

?unmarked
?occu

There are examples on both. Anyhow, I have no trouble fitting the following:

(fm1 <- occu(~1 ~ 1, umf))
(fm2 <- occu(~x3 ~x1, umf))
(fm3 <- occu(~x3+x1 ~x1, umf))

Richard

parts:
Sorry, there is another problem with your data and code. ObsCov defines covariates for each sampling occasion, so if you do two visits to the same place you must have two values of the covariate. However, you only have one value for each site. If the same value applies to the two sampling occasions, then you must add another column with the same data or use it as a site covariate for the purposes of your analyses.

Pablo
